import HartshorneLib.Chapter4CanonicalDivisorSheafBridge

/-!
# A producer for the canonical divisor sheaf

The canonical divisor sheaf is represented by the divisor of a chosen nonzero
rational differential.  This file packages that choice together with the
resulting sheaf.  The choice is part of the data: only the divisor class is
independent of it.  The comparison theorem below is the sheaf-level entry
point for the local regular-differential description of its sections.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry Opposite

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

attribute [local instance] functionFieldOverAlgebra stalkOverAlgebra
  stalkFunctionFieldOver_isScalarTower

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
variable (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral X.left]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom] [IsProper X.hom]

/-- A chosen nonzero rational differential and its associated canonical divisor.

The differential is deliberately stored in the structure, so this producer
does not claim that a particular representative is canonical.
-/
structure CanonicalDivisorSheafProducer where
  differential : CurveRationalDifferentials X
  differential_ne_zero : differential ≠ 0

namespace CanonicalDivisorSheafProducer

variable (P : CanonicalDivisorSheafProducer X)

/-- The divisor represented by the differential selected by `P`. -/
abbrev divisor : CurveDivisor k X :=
  differentialDivisor X P.differential P.differential_ne_zero

/-- The sheaf of bounded rational functions for the selected divisor. -/
noncomputable abbrev sheaf :
    CategoryTheory.Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X.left : TopCat))
      (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
  divisorSheaf P.divisor

@[simp] theorem sheaf_obj (U : X.left.Opens) :
    P.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) = ModuleCat.of k (divisorSections P.divisor U) := rfl

/-- The rational-function value of a section of the produced sheaf. -/
def sectionValue (U : X.left.Opens)
    (s : (P.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) : Type u)) : X.left.functionField := by
  change divisorSections P.divisor U at s
  exact (s : X.left.functionField)

/-- The rational-function value determines a section of the produced sheaf. -/
theorem sectionValue_injective (U : X.left.Opens) :
    Function.Injective (sectionValue (X := X) P U) := by
  intro s t h
  change divisorSections P.divisor U at s t
  change (s : X.left.functionField) = (t : X.left.functionField) at h
  exact Subtype.ext h

/-- Restriction of a bounded section preserves its rational-function value. -/
theorem sectionValue_res
    {U V : X.left.Opens} (h : V ≤ U)
    (hV : (V : Set X.left).Nonempty)
    (s : divisorSections P.divisor U) :
    (divisorSectionsRes P.divisor h s : X.left.functionField) =
      (s : X.left.functionField) := by
  exact divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV s

/- The nonempty-open restriction is detected exactly by the rational-function
   representative.  This is the separatedness input used by later local
   differential comparisons. -/
theorem divisorSectionsRes_injective
    {U V : X.left.Opens} (h : V ≤ U)
    (hV : (V : Set X.left).Nonempty) :
    Function.Injective (divisorSectionsRes P.divisor h) := by
  intro s t hst
  apply Subtype.ext
  have hs := divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV s
  have ht := divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV t
  exact hs.symm.trans ((congrArg Subtype.val hst).trans ht)

theorem divisorSectionsRes_eq_iff
    {U V : X.left.Opens} (h : V ≤ U)
    (hV : (V : Set X.left).Nonempty)
    (s t : divisorSections P.divisor U) :
    divisorSectionsRes P.divisor h s = divisorSectionsRes P.divisor h t ↔
      (s : X.left.functionField) = (t : X.left.functionField) := by
  constructor
  · intro hst
    have hs := divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV s
    have ht := divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV t
    exact hs.symm.trans ((congrArg Subtype.val hst).trans ht)
  · intro hst
    apply Subtype.ext
    rw [divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV, divisorSectionsRes_coe h hV, hst]

/- Multiplication by the selected nonzero differential is cancellable.  The
   differential is choice-dependent data of `P`, so this lemma makes no
   canonicality claim about the resulting coordinate. -/
omit [IsAlgClosed k] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom] [IsProper X.hom] in
theorem regularMultiple_eq_of_differential_eq
    (f g : X.left.functionField)
    (hfg : f • P.differential = g • P.differential) :
    f = g := by
  exact smul_left_injective X.left.functionField P.differential_ne_zero hfg

/-- On a nonempty open, a section of the produced sheaf is regular after
multiplication by the selected rational differential exactly when its value
satisfies the canonical divisor bound. -/
theorem section_mem_iff
    (U : X.left.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X.left).Nonempty)
    (f : X.left.functionField) :
    f ∈ divisorSections P.divisor U ↔
      ∀ (x : X.left) (_hx : x ≠ genericPoint X.left), x ∈ U →
        f • P.differential ∈ curveRegularDifferentialLattice X x := by
  exact mem_divisorSections_differentialDivisor_iff X P.differential
    P.differential_ne_zero U hU f

/-- Every section of the produced sheaf has the regular-differential
description on a nonempty open.  The underlying value is the rational
function represented by the bounded section. -/
theorem sheaf_section_regular
    (U : X.left.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X.left).Nonempty)
    (s : (P.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) : Type u)) :
    ∀ (x : X.left) (_hx : x ≠ genericPoint X.left), x ∈ U →
      sectionValue (X := X) P U s • P.differential ∈
        curveRegularDifferentialLattice X x := by
  change divisorSections P.divisor U at s
  change ∀ (x : X.left) (_hx : x ≠ genericPoint X.left), x ∈ U →
    (s : X.left.functionField) • P.differential ∈
      curveRegularDifferentialLattice X x
  have hs : (s : X.left.functionField) ∈ divisorSections P.divisor U := Subtype.property s
  exact (section_mem_iff (X := X) P U hU (s : X.left.functionField)).mp hs

end CanonicalDivisorSheafProducer

omit [IsAlgClosed k] [IsProper X.hom] in
/-- A smooth proper integral curve admits a canonical-divisor-sheaf producer.

This is an existence statement for choice-dependent data, not a claim that the
selected differential itself is canonical.
-/
theorem exists_canonicalDivisorSheafProducer :
    Nonempty (CanonicalDivisorSheafProducer X) := by
  obtain ⟨ω, hω⟩ := exists_nonzero_curveRationalDifferential X
  exact ⟨⟨ω, hω⟩⟩

end
end Hartshorne
